haha yeah, that definitely doesn't look much like an airbus a320 😂

i tried the exact same prompt here, but lowered the temperature to 0.6, and got this result. still not a perfect a320, of course, but quite a different outcome!

i think adjusting the sampling parameters a bit might help, especially when using more detailed prompts.

the two models also have slightly different focuses. glb-coder was trained mainly for lightweight, low-poly game assets and glb export, while the original 3d-coder focuses more on broader and more complex 3d scenes.

both can handle different types of requests, but their training data definitely influences how they interpret and generate things.

there's still plenty of room for improvement, but i think it's interesting how much the results can vary with just a few adjustments.

thanks for testing and sharing your feedback! it's really helpful for the next versions (:
